newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Pharma Vision sees Hoechst spin-off.
newsitem.headline: Pharma Vision sees Hoechst spin-off.

text.p: Investment trust Pharma Vision said it expects German chemical group Hoechst AG to demerge or spin-off its pharmaceuticals operations into an independent unit within the next two years.
Peter Sjoestroem, member of the board of Pharma Vision, told a news conference he expected major rises in the shares of Hoechst when such a demerger takes place.
Pharma Vision, one of the world's largest trusts specialised in investing in health care companies, last year invested 196.3 million Swiss francs in acquiring 0.5 percent of Hoechst bearer shares.
The investment was financed by a sale of some of Pharma Vision's stake in Roche Holding AG.
Pharma Vision said it took the stake in Hoechst in light of the reorganisation under new management, which has led to "an impressive transformation in the past three years."
Sjoestroem said Hoechst's pharma unit should be given the best possible conditions to operate under and it should be two years maximum before a spin-off takes place.
In February Hoechst said one of the options under consideration was making the pharma operations independent.
Sjoestroem said the best solution for Hoechst would be to make its pharma operations independent.
